first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ, which directly threatens sustainable revenue. Memory_91 shows in-product activation messaging improved week-one engagement and nudged accounts to first action—this is the highest-leverage lever available given current metrics. Memory_86 supports that time-to-value improvements drive adoption. Promotional pricing (memory_73) would address the SMB price-sensitive segment but risks margin erosion and doesn't address the core activation decline. Onboarding simplification (memory_31) is proven effective, but activation decline is the larger immediate metric drag. Referral incentives (memory_57) are suited for revenue expansion among established customers, not solving current acquisition/activation friction. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is high-value but addresses a different segment and doesn't solve self-serve activation headwinds. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm the strength of both onboarding and activation levers before committing. Activation messaging targets the specific QoQ decline directly and builds on proven mechanics.
